mMPLQuoteBlocking.analysis: The MMPL does not forbid derivation, so the task's precondition 'if the licence forbids reuse, say so explicitly' is not triggered in those words. But it is not a permissive licence either: a distributed derivative of the source must be non-revenue-generating (line 99), must credit the Author (line 100) and must itself comply with the MMPL (line 101). Condition 101 is the operative blocker: it means a derivative incorporating MMPL code cannot simply be relicensed under whatever licence Minecraft Historical Experience uses; the derivative would have to carry a compatible mod licence and keep the Mod name right with the Author (line 135). Line 136 ('cannot do so retroactively') means the later LGPL grant, even if it were intended to cover the source, could not retroactively free code authored under the MMPL.

Interpretation was joined from the mod's own en_us.json resource (2095 keys) by camel-casing the constant and looking up gui.nostalgic_tweaks.config.<category>.<camel>, and from the mixin registration manifests common/src/main/resources/mixin.nostalgic_tweaks.json and mixin.nostalgic_tweaks-required.json.
inventorySummary.sideSemantics: The side is read from the factory call in the declaration itself: `.client(...)`, `.server(...)` or `.dynamic(...)`. 'dynamic' means the mod synchronises the value between client and server, so it is not purely one side.

sourceScopingFinding.finding: This mod reads its tweaks from a static, process-global configuration object, not from world state.
evidence: Tweak declarations are `static final` interface fields, e.g. GameplayTweak.DISABLE_HUNGER at mod/adrenix/nostalgic/tweak/config/GameplayTweak.java:204, and every implementation site gates on that static, e.g. mod/adrenix/nostalgic/mixin/tweak/gameplay/food_health/FoodDataMixin.java:34 (`if (GameplayTweak.DISABLE_HUNGER.get())`) and FoodDataMixin.java:55.

Configuration is persisted per client and per server as JSON files in the mod-loader config directory, not per world: mod/adrenix/nostalgic/config/ServerConfig.java:32 annotates the structure with @Config(filename = NostalgicTweaks.MOD_ID + "-server"), and mod/adrenix/nostalgic/config/factory/ConfigHandler.java:100-106 documents that 'The config file will be kept in the default config folder used by mod loaders'.
sourceScopingFinding.consequenceForHX: This is the single most important architectural difference between the two projects. Nostalgic Tweaks answers 'what should this world do' from ambient global configuration; Minecraft Historical Experience requires every rule to be resolved from the world or generator itself so that different historical versions can run side by side in one server (see VersionRules javadoc at src/main/java/net/historicalexperience/version/HistoricalVersion.java:150-161 noting that empty collections 'leave the modern behaviour alone', and HistoricalPlayerRules.java:15-16 which states the hook 'asks the registry what this version does'). Every NT behaviour is therefore only directly reusable as an ALGORITHM, never as a configuration mechanism. This is recorded once here and referenced by every adaptation classification below.

features.name: Disable sprinting
sourceFiles: common/src/main/java/mod/adrenix/nostalgic/mixin/tweak/gameplay/stamina_sprint/PlayerMixin.java:15-55 (stamina persistence, unrelated to the sprint flag itself)
features.historicalBoundary: Pre-Beta 1.8 (no sprint at all). NT expresses this as 'old'/'disable', not as a version string.
features.evidence: NT's own config description for DISABLE_SPRINT (en_us.json gui.nostalgic_tweaks.config.gameplay.disableSprint.info) says only 'Disables the ability for the player to sprint. This tweak is only applied in survival mode.' and names NO version. The boundary is inferred from the tweak's framing as a restoration of old behaviour plus the mod's overall Alpha/Beta scope, not asserted. No comment, enum or constant in the source names Beta 1.8 for this. Separately and independently, the consuming project already records that 'the b1.8.1 jar's sprint fingerprint could not be located, so Beta 1.8 added sprinting is documented version history rather than a jar observation' (src/main/java/net/historicalexperience/version/HistoricalVersions.java:126-128) — that is HX's own primary-source status, and NT adds no primary evidence beyond it.
features.secondarySourceCaveat: Nostalgic Tweaks asserts no boundary here at all. Its implementation is evidence about how NT behaves, not about when the original game changed.
features.adaptationNote: NOT APPLICABLE — ALREADY IMPLEMENTED in the consuming project, and implemented more strictly than NT's approach. HX cancels only the request to START sprinting (src/main/java/net/historicalexperience/mixin/LivingEntityHistoricalSprintMixin.java:29-52, which returns early when sprinting==false) and resolves the version from the world the player is in. NT instead rewrites the boolean argument outright and, notably, lets creative and spectator players sprint unconditionally (mechanics_player/LivingEntityMixin.java:39-41). NT's version is NOT a candidate for adaptation.
features.notes: Already implemented in HX and implemented more strictly; listed only to close the task's priority topic. NT exempts creative and spectator, which HX does not.

features.name: Disable the hunger system and convert food to direct healing
features.historicalBoundary: Beta 1.8 (hunger added; before it, food healed directly). NT never states the version.
features.evidence: The description (en_us.json gui.nostalgic_tweaks.config.gameplay.disableHunger.info) is 'All consumed food will give hearts instead of hunger. The hunger bar will be hidden when this tweak's effects are active. To change the amount of health restored by foods, edit the gameplay.customFoodHealth list.' No version named. The consuming project independently treats hunger as a Beta 1.8 arrival and cites b1.8.1 client evidence for a 'FoodStats-shaped hunger class' (src/main/java/net/historicalexperience/version/HistoricalVersions.java:123-125); NT contributes nothing to that.
features.secondarySourceCaveat: NT's boundary framing is 'old' only. Its behavioural evidence is strong and interesting (see adaptationNote) but is evidence about NT.
features.adaptationNote: ADAPTABLE WITH A NEW SHARED HOOK, and this is the single most valuable finding of the audit for HX. HX currently CANCELS FoodData.tick entirely (src/main/java/net/historicalexperience/mixin/FoodDataHistoricalHungerMixin.java:38-51) and its own javadoc at HistoricalPlayerRules.java:28-31 records this as a known gap: 'Beta 1.7.3 healed directly when the player ate. That is not implemented yet ... eating also does not yet heal.' NT supplies the mechanism HX is missing. NT does NOT replace tick; it lets tick run and instead: (a) heals directly in Player.eat (PlayerMixin.java:29-42), computing the amount as the item's modern FoodProperties.nutrition unless a per-item override exists, and (b) zeroes exhaustionLevel and tickTimer at the head of FoodData.tick (FoodDataMixin.java:55-60) so no drain, regeneration or starvation occurs while retaining the method's other behaviour. CRITICAL COMPATIBILITY FACT: NT's secondary heal path is inside FoodData.tick itself (FoodDataMixin.java:43-53, healing from a stored nt$restoreHealthAmount), so if HX keeps cancelling tick, that path is dead. HX should adopt the Player.eat-side heal (which is outside tick) rather than the tick-side one. Also worth noting: NT's heal amount defaults to the modern nutrition value, and its override map only lists the items whose modern nutrition differs — see the foodHealingValues feature below.
features.notes: Highest-value finding for HX. NT reaches the eat path from Player.eat, which is OUTSIDE FoodData.tick, so HX can adopt healing without abandoning its cancellation. Do not uncancel tick to get healing.

features.name: Per-item food heal amounts under no-hunger
features.historicalBoundary: UNKNOWN as a version; the values are a curated list, not a version-scoped table.
features.evidence: DefaultListing.foodHealth() (lines 112-128) sets a base value of 10 for every edible item and then overrides: rotten flesh 0, spider eye 0, carrot 1, melon slice 1, chorus fruit 1, sweet berries 1, glow berries 1, mushroom stew 10, beetroot soup 10, rabbit stew 10, suspicious stew 10, golden apple 20, enchanted golden apple 20. NO comment in DefaultListing.java states where any of these numbers come from, and no version is attributed. PlayerMixin.java:38-41 shows the resolution rule: modern nutrition, overridden by the map entry when present.
features.secondarySourceCaveat: Because no provenance is given for the numbers, they are NT's own claim and must not be treated as Beta 1.7.3 values. This matters directly: HX's HistoricalPlayerRules.java:30-31 says direct healing 'needs Beta's per-item heal amounts verified from the client, which has not been done', and NT does not supply that verification.
features.adaptationNote: DIRECTLY ADAPTABLE AS A VERSION RULE — the shape fits HX's rule table exactly (a map of item id to integer, keyed by version, expressed as data). However the VALUES must not be trusted: they are uncited secondary-source data. Use the shape, and populate it from HX's own hash-verified Beta 1.7.3 client evidence as HistoricalLootRules.java:56-65 does for drops. Note also the model difference: NT expresses this as a sparse override over modern nutrition; HX's existing loot model prefers an explicit complete table, and an explicit table avoids inheriting anachronistic modern values for items whose override is missing.
features.notes: Shape is reusable; the numbers are uncited and must be re-derived. NT expresses it as a sparse override over modern nutrition, which silently inherits modern values for unlisted items; HX should prefer an explicit complete table.

features.name: Food is only edible when the player is below full health
features.historicalBoundary: UNKNOWN — no version stated.
features.evidence: No comment or lang string attributes this to a version. It follows logically from direct healing (if food heals rather than feeds, eating at full health is pointless) and is presented in source as part of the DISABLE_HUNGER behaviour, but no boundary is asserted.
features.secondarySourceCaveat: No boundary claim to caveat.
features.adaptationNote: DIRECTLY ADAPTABLE AS A VERSION RULE, but should be treated as part of the same rule as direct food healing, not a separate version parameter. It is one line of behaviour (compare ceil(health) < ceil(maxHealth)) and needs no new hook — it belongs on the same Player.eat hook the feature above requires. Flag for the parent: this is a behavioural consequence HX has not yet decided on, and adopting direct healing without it would let a player waste food.
features.notes: Behavioural consequence of direct healing rather than an independent historical rule; belongs on the same hook. Flagged so the parent can decide, since adopting healing without it lets a player waste food.

features.name: Instantaneous eating
features.historicalBoundary: UNKNOWN — no version stated.
features.evidence: No comment, enum or lang string names a version for instantaneous eating. The description is 'Eating food is now instant.'
features.secondarySourceCaveat: No boundary claim to caveat.
features.adaptationNote: ADAPTABLE WITH A NEW SHARED HOOK. Suppressing the eat duration is not expressible in HX's current VersionRules (five booleans, a spawn set and a drop map), and it requires touching item use duration rather than a boolean. It is also genuinely a bundle: NT pairs it with sound suppression (food_health/LivingEntityMixin.java:28-36), effect suppression (LivingEntityMixin.java:40-48), a client re-equip animation change (food_health/MinecraftMixin.java:22-40) and a client movement-stutter fix (food_health/LocalPlayerMixin.java:24-36), of which the last two are client-only. Classified b rather than c because the server rule itself is a single coherent behaviour, but the parent should scope it carefully: the server-side half is separable from the client presentation half.
features.notes: A bundle, not one rule: server-side duration plus sound and effect suppression, and a client-only animation change and movement-stutter fix. The server half is separable from the client half.

features.adaptationNote: NOT APPLICABLE for the current registry. Every version HX declares predates the cooldown's introduction, so the modern cooldown is an anachronism that would be WRONG to disable via a version rule if it is present at all in the target runtime. If HX's target Minecraft version has a cooldown and a declared historical version must not, the correct HX action is a version rule saying 'this version has no cooldown', which is a NEW rule not covered by NT's global flag semantics. Recorded so it is not silently dropped.
features.notes: Out of range for every currently declared version. If the runtime has a cooldown and a declared version must not, that is a NEW rule NT's global flag cannot express.

features.name: Remove critical hits
features.historicalBoundary: Beta 1.8 (critical hits arrived with the Adventure Update).
features.evidence: The description is 'Removes the ability for players to perform critical hit attacks.' No version named. The boundary is inferred from the consuming project's own registry shape, which groups critical-hit-era mechanics with Beta 1.8, not from any NT statement.
features.secondarySourceCaveat: NT asserts no boundary. Additionally, NT's IMPLEMENTATION MECHANISM is notable and slightly alarming: it fakes a climbable state (PlayerMixin.java:62-66 returns true from the onClimbable expression) to defeat the vanilla critical-hit precondition. That is a clever trick for a global flag but a poor fit for a rule engine that must not have side effects on other climbability consumers.

features.name: Old animal spawning algorithm and cap
features.historicalBoundary: Alpha/Beta — explicitly stated by NT.
features.evidence: NT states the boundary in the config description: en_us.json gui.nostalgic_tweaks.config.gameplay.animalSpawnCap.info reads 'Controls how many groups of animals can spawn around a player when gameplay.oldAnimalSpawning is enabled. A higher cap yields more animals. This only applies to animals defined in the gameplay.oldAnimalSpawnList tweak. To simulate alpha and beta spawn rates, set this value to 15.' The default is 15 (GameplayTweak.java:59), i.e. the shipped default is the stated Alpha/Beta value. The default spawn list is chicken, cow, mooshroom, pig, sheep (DefaultListing.java:84-88). The implemented algorithm is in AnimalSpawnHelper: 17x17 chunks polled around each player (lines 84-91), a cap test of ANIMAL_SPAWN_CAP * chunks/256 (line 110), 3 outer attempts each with up to 4 inner placements (lines 126-133), a 24-block exclusion around the world spawn point computed as a squared distance of 576 (lines 165-174), a light-level floor of > 8 (lines 241-242), list membership and canSummon (line 246), SpawnPlacements.checkSpawnRules and a noCollision AABB test (lines 249-252).
features.secondarySourceCaveat: NT's 'to simulate alpha and beta spawn rates, set this value to 15' is an assertion with no citation. The algorithm's structure is strong evidence that NT reconstructed the old logic deliberately, but it is still a reconstruction by a third party, not the original code.
features.adaptationNote: GENUINELY A DIFFERENT ALGORITHM — MUST NOT BE FORCED INTO THE RULE TABLE. This is the single most important classification in the audit. HX's existing spawn work is an ALLOW-LIST FILTER over candidate entries (HistoricalSpawnFilter applied from NaturalSpawnerHistoricalSpawnMixin.java:48-82, and HistoricalSpawnRules.java:122-124 isAllowed). NT's old animal spawning does not filter at all: it REPLACES the spawning algorithm, running its own chunk polling loop, its own cap arithmetic, its own attempts-per-chunk and pack logic, its own light and spawn-distance rules, and it separately alters entity persistence (removeWhenFarAway overrides, and the persistent-baby marking in AnimalSpawnHelper.isPersistent at lines 61-64). Forcing that into HX's allow-list table would be exactly the 'fundamentally different algorithm in a simple configuration table' failure the project's core rule forbids. Recommendation: the allow LIST is class-a data (it is just a set of entity ids and could even be subsumed by HX's existing allowedNaturalSpawns), but the ALGORITHM must be a separate subsystem with its own design, and its cap/attempt constants should be version data feeding that algorithm rather than a VersionRules boolean.
features.boundaryStatusDetail: NT states the boundary in the animalSpawnCap description. The underlying history is NT's assertion; the default of 15 is the value NT says simulates Alpha and Beta.
features.notes: Most important classification in the audit. The allow LIST is class-a data and may be subsumed by allowedNaturalSpawns; the ALGORITHM is class c and must not be forced into the rule table. Split accordingly.

recommendations.feature: Direct food healing for no-hunger versions (the mechanism, not NT's numbers)
recommendations.boundary: Beta 1.7.3 and earlier: food heals hearts directly and there is no hunger bar. Boundary status for HX purposes: HX already treats hunger as a Beta 1.8 arrival with b1.8.1 client evidence (HistoricalVersions.java:123-125), so the 'before Beta 1.8' side of the boundary is HX's own; NT adds no boundary.
recommendations.evidence: NT's mechanism: heal on Player.eat (mixin/tweak/gameplay/food_health/PlayerMixin.java:29-42) using the item's nutrition unless a per-item override exists (PlayerMixin.java:38-41), plus zeroing exhaustionLevel and tickTimer at the head of FoodData.tick (FoodDataMixin.java:55-60) rather than cancelling tick, plus allowing eating only below full health (PlayerMixin.java:49-60). HX's current gap is documented in its own source: HistoricalPlayerRules.java:28-31.
recommendations.proposingTest: Pure unit test first, mirroring the project's existing null-object style: assert that for the Beta 1.7.3 profile and a player at less than full health, eating a known food raises health by the profile's declared heal amount and leaves foodLevel/exhaustionLevel at their pre-eat values; then an integration test in run/ that a Beta 1.7.3 world and a Beta 1.8.1 world loaded in the SAME server show different behaviour for the same food item, which is the invariant HX's architecture exists to guarantee. A negative test must confirm an ordinary (non-historical) world is unaffected.
recommendations.alreadyImplementedDetail: The hunger-has-no-effect half is implemented (FoodDataHistoricalHungerMixin.java cancels FoodData.tick). The healing half is explicitly NOT implemented. IMPORTANT: any adoption must not simply uncancel tick, because HX's existing suppression and the project's per-world gating were designed around cancellation; the correct change is to heal from the eat path, which NT shows is available outside tick.

recommendations.boundary: Alpha/Beta, as asserted by NT. Zombie 0.23 and spider 0.3 are explicitly excluded by NT as unchanged.
recommendations.evidence: This is one of the few boundaries NT states in words: en_us.json gui.nostalgic_tweaks.config.gameplay.oldMobSpeeds.info. The data shape is a per-entity double map with a fallback (tweak/listing/DefaultListing.java:63-78) and the tweak is server-side (GameplayTweak.java:31-34).
recommendations.proposingTest: Unit test asserting the declared speed for each entity in a Beta profile and the fallback for an unlisted entity, plus an integration test that a mob spawned in a Beta world reports the historical movement-speed attribute while the same entity type in a Beta 1.8.1 or ordinary world reports the modern value. Because NT's numbers are uncited, the acceptance criterion should be that the values come from an HX-verified source, and the test should fail loudly if a value is still marked provisional.
recommendations.alreadyImplementedDetail: HX has mob DROPS and natural SPAWN restrictions, but no movement-speed or attribute data of any kind. This is a clean new rule with an existing map shape to copy.

recommendations.feature: Block/entity interaction restrictions (left-click door/lever/button; disable axe stripping and shovel pathing)
recommendations.boundary: UNKNOWN from NT — no version is stated for any of the five toggles. NT's framing is 'disable' (these are modern conveniences), and axe stripping and shovel pathing both postdate Release 1.7.10.
recommendations.evidence: GameplayTweak.java:143-145 (three server-side booleans) and GameplayTweak.java:199-200 (two dynamic booleans); InteractionHelper.java:16-29 shows the technique of reading the vanilla flattenables/strippables maps through accessor mixins rather than hard-coding block lists.
recommendations.proposingTest: Integration test in run/: in a historical world, right-click a log with an axe and assert the block is unchanged and no sound plays; left-click a door and assert it opens subject to the rate limit; then repeat both in an ordinary world and assert vanilla behaviour. The negative path is essential here because a mis-scoped interaction hook is the classic way an emulation mod breaks ordinary worlds.
recommendations.alreadyImplementedDetail: HX currently has NO interaction-restriction mixin at all (the mixin package holds only feature-placer, ore, loot, sprint, hunger and natural-spawn mixins). This would be the first, which is why it is ranked below the two data-only items.
recommendations.implementationCaution: Do not copy NT's accessor-map technique blindly; read the maps so the restriction tracks the runtime's own data, but the rate limit NT applies to left-click interaction is stateful and needs an explicit design decision.

recommendations.feature: Per-version numeric spawn caps and spawn-parameter data
recommendations.boundary: UNKNOWN. NT states only that the vanilla monster cap is 70 and that animal spawn cap 15 'simulates alpha and beta spawn rates'.
recommendations.evidence: GameplayTweak.java:48-51 (MONSTER_SPAWN_CAP default 90, overriding MobCategory.getMaxInstancesPerChunk via mixin/tweak/gameplay/monster_spawn/MobCategoryMixin.java:27-28) and GameplayTweak.java:59 with the animalSpawnCap lang string.
recommendations.proposingTest: A bounded integration test that spawns a historical world, counts naturally-spawned monsters per player over a fixed number of ticks, and asserts the count stays within the profile's declared cap while an ordinary world is unchanged. The test must assert the cap is applied through the world-derived version, not a global, which is the exact failure mode NT's architecture would import into HX.
recommendations.alreadyImplementedDetail: HX restricts WHICH entity types may spawn (HistoricalSpawnRules allow list), not HOW MANY. Caps are a genuinely new parameter class. Ranked below interaction restrictions because the historical cap semantics for Beta 1.7.3 and Beta 1.8.1 are not established in HX's own evidence base and would need research before the parameter can be trusted.
recommendations.implementationCaution: Do NOT adopt NT's animal spawning algorithm here — see rank-5 note and the old-animal-spawning feature, which is class c. Only the numeric parameter is proposed.

recommendations.feature: Combat critical-hit and cooldown gating expressed as version rules
recommendations.boundary: Post-Release 1.7.10 / post-Beta 1.8. NT states NO boundary for either; the boundary follows from HX's version range instead.
recommendations.evidence: GameplayTweak.java:103 (DISABLE_COOLDOWN) and GameplayTweak.java:105 (DISABLE_CRITICAL_HIT), both server-side; enforcement at mixin/tweak/gameplay/combat_player/PlayerMixin.java:26-51 (cooldown) and PlayerMixin.java:53-67 (critical hit, implemented by faking a climbable result).
recommendations.proposingTest: Unit test that the profile flags resolve correctly per version, plus an integration test that a critical hit does not occur in a Beta 1.7.3 world while it does in an ordinary world, and that the same player attacking from a LADDER in an ordinary world still behaves correctly — that last case is the specific regression NT's climbable-faking trick would risk in HX, which is why the test must cover it.
recommendations.alreadyImplementedDetail: Nothing in this area is implemented. It is ranked last of the five because its boundary is inferred rather than stated, its enforcement mechanism must deliberately NOT be copied, and the practical impact inside HX's current version range is small (critical hits and the cooldown both postdate most declared versions).

recommendationsExplicitlyNotProposed.reason: Already implemented in HX from stronger evidence (HistoricalLootRules.java:56-65 cites the hash-verified b1.7.3 client per mob). NT's equivalent is uncited, uses a uniform count distribution rather than nextInt(3), and adds a looting multiplier Beta 1.7.3 did not have. Two gaps NT incidentally reveals are recorded as follow-ups in that feature row, not as adaptations.

Already implemented, and HX's implementation is stricter and better scoped than NT's (HX blocks only the start request and does not exempt creative/spectator; NT rewrites the boolean and exempts creative and spectator).

Not a historical Minecraft feature; it is a mod-authored mechanic with per-player NBT state and a dynamic global flag. Adopting it would mean inventing gameplay, and its state model conflicts with HX's world-derived rule resolution.
Belong in the future client package by the project's own separation of concerns, and reproducing them would require historical assets HX may not be able to redistribute.

Deliberately NOT proposed despite being high-impact, because it is class c: it replaces the spawning algorithm with its own chunk polling, cap arithmetic, attempts-per-chunk, light floor, spawn-distance rule and persistence overrides (AnimalSpawnHelper.java:73-253 plus removeWhenFartherAway overrides). unknowns.unknown: Precise Minecraft version boundaries for the overwhelming majority of the 527 tweaks.
unknowns.why: NT encodes boundaries in prose, not in structured data. A scan of the whole en_us.json (2095 keys) found only 78 values mentioning any version-like token, and a scan of the mixin tree found exactly one version token in a code comment. There is no version-tagged schema, no per-tweak boundary field, and no preset that maps to a specific Minecraft version. Most tweaks are labelled only 'old' or 'classic', and where a boundary IS stated it is usually at era granularity (Classic, Alpha, Beta) rather than a version number.
unknowns.whatWouldSettleIt: Primary evidence from the original game clients (which is what HX's own research already does and what makes NT insufficient as a source for boundaries), or an upstream NT release that adds structured boundary metadata.

methodology.primarySourcesOnly: Every claim in this audit is sourced to the cloned repository's own files, its git history objects, its own resource files, or its own build metadata. External web pages were used ONLY to establish the canonical repository URL and to test whether the requested URL exists. No wiki, README marketing text, forum post or third-party summary was used as evidence for any behaviour or boundary.
methodology.readmeExplicitlyNotUsedForFeatures: The feature inventory was built from the six config declaration classes and cross-checked against the mod's own mixin registration manifests, deliberately NOT from README.md as the task required.
methodology.noCodeCopied: No source file, asset or texture was copied into the deliverables. Findings are expressed as file:line citations and behavioural descriptions, per the project's instruction not to copy proprietary code or textures into deliverables.
methodology.nothingExecuted: No build, Gradle task, Minecraft launch, test suite or mod run was performed. All findings come from reading source, resource files and git objects. Consequently every adaptation proposal is a design proposal and has NOT been runtime-verified; the proposingTest fields describe tests that would need to be written and run.
methodology.cloneNotModified: The clone at .upstream/nostalgic-tweaks was used read-only. `git status --porcelain` on it returns empty. Deep reading used a separate worktree outside the repository tree.
methodology.boundaryStatusSemantics: VERIFIED means the mod's own source, resource or enum states the boundary, and the citation is given; it does NOT mean the boundary is historically true. INFERRED means the auditor concluded it from structure or context and says why. UNKNOWN means no boundary could be established and the search performed is recorded. Every row also names what NT's claim is evidence ABOUT.

parentCorrection.whyTheWorkerAndParentDisagree: The audit correctly described the audited BRANCH and the parent initially over-generalised that to the PROJECT, concluding copying was forbidden. The project's declared licence, on the default branch and on its distribution page, is LGPL-3.0-only. obligationsIfCodeIsReused: Any distributed derivative containing Nostalgic Tweaks code must itself be licensed LGPL-3.0-only; this workspace currently has no LICENSE file, so that is an explicit decision for the project owner before any distribution
Copyright notices and the licence text must be retained
Modified files must carry prominent notices stating that they were changed
LGPL is weak copyleft, not permissive: it is not sufficient to merely attribute
This project's own contract already forbids shipping proprietary Minecraft code or assets, which is unaffected by the upstream licence
parentCorrection.practicalConsequence: Copying is permitted, but the architecture mismatch still decides the approach: Nostalgic Tweaks reads a process-global static config while this project resolves the version from the world, and ~80% of its tweaks are client-only with no client package here yet. Values, tables and algorithms remain the useful part, and they are reimplemented against our own world-derived gate either way. Where a class is copied verbatim, the LGPL obligations above apply and THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md must record it.
